FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Sign shape and color announce their job: regulation signs are normally white rectangles with black or red markings, warnings yellow diamonds with black, destinations green with white, and services blue with white. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=29]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
The red-and-white stop sign demands a full stop with right-of-way yielded, halting before the stop line, else the crosswalk, else the nearest point with a clear view into the intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=29]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
The red-and-white yield sign demands slowing, traffic checks and readiness to stop, a full stop whenever conditions require, and yielded right-of-way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=29]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Other regulation signs rule direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking and special cases, with a red circle-and-slash banning the pictured action or vehicle and rectangular white signs flagging special rules. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=29]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A02
Yellow-and-black warnings mark hazards and special rules, sometimes paired with a yellow-and-black advisory speed urging slower travel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=30]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A02
Orange-and-black work signs mark active work with possible flag control and work limits as low as twenty-five, and drivers slow through every work zone and obey every flag signal with or without a posted limit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=30]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A02
Green-and-white destination signs give direction and distance, while varied route markers name interstate, United States, state or county roads by shape, in sample order state, United States, interstate, for map planning and en-route tracking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=30]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A02
Blue-and-white service signs point to rest areas, fuel, camping and medical help. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=30]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A02
Signals normally stack red, yellow and green top-to-bottom or left-to-right, appearing lone, flashing, round or arrowed, and dead or broken signals force a stop-sign stop followed by right-of-way rules unless an officer directs otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=30]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A03
Steady red means stop until green, or arrow-only movement on a green arrow when clear; right on red and one-way-to-one-way left on red are allowed after a full stop with yielding, except where signs, signals or markings forbid, anywhere unposted in the city, and right on red never for a school bus carrying students. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=31]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A03
Flashing red equals a stop sign with stop, yield and safe-go, while a red arrow bans all movement its way until it clears, including any turn on red. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=31]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A03
Steady yellow warns of imminent red with stopping preparation, flashing yellow orders caution, and a yellow arrow ends green-arrow protection with stopping preparation for intending turners. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=31]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A03
Steady green and green arrows both permit movement while still yielding right-of-way as the law requires. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=31]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A03
Overhead lane lights ban the lane on a steady red X, order exit on a steady yellow X, restrict to left turns on a flashing yellow X, and open the lane on a green arrow. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=31]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A03
Road paint divides lanes, gates passing and lane changes, assigns turn lanes and stop points; edge lines mark the shoulder boundary that crossing breaks except by official order or sign, and an inward-angling edge line warns of narrowing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=31]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A04
White divides same-direction lanes and yellow divides opposing flows in solid or broken pairs, and one broken line allows passing or lane changes when safe and non-interfering. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=32]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A04
Beside a solid-and-broken pair, the solid side bans passing and crossing except for a left into a driveway, while the broken side passes when safe and non-interfering. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=32]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A04
Double solid lines ban passing, lane changes and crossing except to turn left entering or leaving the road or to U-turn, while a single solid line allows passing and changes only when obstructions or traffic force it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=32]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A04
Signed or signaled intersections may paint a white stop line or parallel crosswalk lines, stopping falls before whichever exists only when a device, officer or yielding pedestrian, skater or scooter user demands it, and set-back single lines shelter truck turning room. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=32]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A04
Lane arrows dictate lane use, such as right-only from the right lane and straight-only from the left, with lane choice settled before the solid separator. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=32]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A05
Diamond lanes reserve for buses, high-occupancy vehicles, bicycles and posted specials during posted times, with city broken-white gaps admitting non-carpool right turns at the next corner, all to speed the highest-value traffic. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=33]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A05
Officer directions beat every sign, signal and marking, including stop-on-green and go-on-red orders, from police, fire police, work flaggers, crossing persons and school bus drivers. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=33]
